interactions.summary: Greg asks Jiang to explain the counterintuitive claim that Israel, Saudi Arabia, and Iran can all benefit from America being dragged deeper into Middle Eastern war.

Jiang gives a two-layer answer: first, America has an economic incentive to dominate oil flows because of debt and treasury dependence; second, deeper religious factions inside the national-security apparatus want a Middle East war to fulfill eschatological prophecy and build toward Gog and Magog, the third temple, and world-government scenarios.
Greg then asks whether China or the East has any parallel history of power organized around inherited prophecy, or whether this style of elite eschatology is uniquely Western or Abrahamic.

claims.claim: Jiang says America's debt dependence makes control of global oil supply strategically attractive because it helps preserve demand for U.S. treasuries and leverage over other economies.
Jiang argues that if America controlled Iran, Venezuela, and allied Gulf oil, it could dictate energy prices to China, Japan, South Korea, and Europe.

Jiang says a deeper driver than economics is eschatological: Christian Zionists, evangelicals, Freemasons, Mormons, Jesuits, and religious extremist Jews all want Middle East war because they see it as prophecy fulfillment.
claims.temporal_scope: Diagnostic claim about present power structures on 2025-10-07.

claims.claim: Jiang says these religious factions want a Middle East war because they believe it can produce Gog and Magog, the return of messianic figures, and some form of world government.
claims.temporal_scope: Diagnostic claim about present eschatological motives on 2025-10-07.

claims.claim: Jiang suggests this prophetic program may stretch back to America's founding and connect through later events such as JFK and 9/11.
Jiang predicts the Al-Aqsa Mosque will be destroyed within six months to a year and says that from his model this destruction would be fundamental to third-temple prophecy and wider war.
claims.temporal_scope: Prediction for roughly late 2025 to late 2026, made on 2025-10-07.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang calls the American economy a giant Ponzi scheme that needs fresh treasury buyers to keep moving.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It condenses his economic diagnosis into a harsh image that links debt management to imperial compulsion.

signature_moments.moment: The war planners are not improvising; to them the apocalypse is a script.
signature_moments.source_phrase: it's almost like a script to them
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This preserves Jiang's central claim that theology, not just interest calculation, is structuring strategic behavior.

signature_moments.moment: The factions pushing war are like marathon runners who can finally see the finish line and will kill themselves climbing the last mountain to reach it.
signature_moments.source_phrase: they finally see the finish line
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It gives the eschatological rush a vivid tempo: desperation rises because prophecy is felt as near, not abstract.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang's term for power behavior driven by end-times prophecy rather than normal strategic or economic reasoning.
The apocalyptic war scenario Jiang says multiple religious factions want to trigger through Middle East escalation.
The temple Jiang says prophecy-minded actors want to build after Al-Aqsa's destruction.

chronology_notes.note: This packet contains one of the interview's sharpest dated predictions: Jiang explicitly puts Al-Aqsa destruction on a six-month-to-one-year horizon from 2025-10-07.

uncertainty_notes.note: The JFK and 9/11 linkage is presented as a possible extension of the prophecy thesis rather than a fully argued proof in this packet, so it is recorded with medium confidence.
